Error in nlminb(obj$par, obj$fn, obj$gr, control = obj$control) :
  (converted from warning) NA/NaN function evaluation

I have been chasing this error for about a week. I does serve to occupy my shelter in place time, but is really annoying. I cannot find any clue that leads me to the source of this error. I have looked in the TMB Dox and search this group to no avail.

None of my usual tactics to solve this sort of problem seem to be feasible. The math.h function isnan(...) does not seem to be applicable to and instance of class Type, nor can a Type variable be easily cast to a double. Also it does not seem possible to create an ofstream object in my cpp file.

Oddly enough the parameter values coughed up by obj.report() seem reasonable, so I'm optimistic about the model. That said, I'm willing to acknowledge that my model is ill-posed and that the data are not informative. But to make that determination it seems necessary to pinpoint the source of the NA/NaN error.

messages.author: 78c4b7b5f6907d81
messages.subject: Re: NA/NaN function evaluation
parts:
There is a trick in TMB to check if a value is NaN.
Currently in C++, comparisons with a NaN return FALSE, with an exception.
The comparison !=, when either or both operands is NaN returns TRUE.
That means x != x returns TRUE only if x is NaN.

Hope it helps.

parts:
Hi Timothee,

Thanks for the creative suggestion. I encapsulated your idea in my own
isNaN(...) function as follows:

> template < class Type > Type isNaN(Type x, const int line)
> {
>     if (x != x)
>     {
>          std::cerr << "NaN at line " << line << std::endl;
>          exit(1);
>     }
>     return x;
> }
which can be called as       f += isNaN(nll,__LINE__);

Alas, it executes as expected, but did not uncover my particular NaN. I
guess I need to look deeper.

Cheers,

John

I forgot to mention how to make sure your NaN detection works as expected.
You should be able to declare a NaN variable this way:
double mynanvar = std::numeric_limits<double>::quiet_NaN();

However, Kasper's nan debugging looks handier than manually checking every variable.

Good luck
